column4: A luonnotar his early 50's. He is plain, quiet, forgettable. He is immune to all magic. And has an incredible ability purge a person of all magical ability forever.
The unassuming Grigori hero combined the abilities of a Luonnotar and Runewyn, and has unequaled abilities in Force Magic.

Tomb Wardens are minor Angels whom Arawn (when he was God of Life as well as Death, before Sucellus claimed the mantle that first belonged to Nemed) tasked with guarding the passages that lead out from the Netherworld into Erebus. They are responsible for guiding new souls into the bodies of unborn babes, and helping children struggle through the first years of life in a world full of deadly diseases. Most continue to fill that role under the command of Sucellus, but many shirk their duties in order to assume jobs better suited for the Dullahan. These angels are as often found near the exits of Erebus as its entrances. They guide spirits of the dead out of Erebus, lest they be abducted by demons to join the great machine or hell of left to languish in an increasing state of corruption. Wardens specialize in slaying the Undead, but prefer to strike down potential Necromancers before they can raise such abominations. Most of what mortals know of Tomb Wardens come from tales told by grave robbers who narrowly escaped with their lives.

Tomb Wardens are strong against the Undead, and like the Undead can emerge to punish those who rob graveyards. They are most likely to defend Graveyards on Hallowed Ground, and their appearance in such graveyards extends the duration of the Hallowing there.

Created during the Age of Dragons, Djinn are strengthened by magical energy. They were Oghma's attempt to use the power of the other gods against them. Djinn are amorphous blue forms, though they usually choose to appear as humanoids, like men made of flowing water. In an environment without magic they become weak and sedentary. Their nature makes it impossible to imprison them in magical traps or bars, but in environments without magic they can be held in items as simple as tightly corked bottles.

Djinn are magic-immune summons with all the powers of Archmages. They are gifted affinity in one or two random spheres, based on your effective mana supply, allowing them to cast the greater versions of the spells from those spheres. The Tower of the Elements may grant them free promotion picks based on your effective supply of Metamagic mana.

An Adept with enough experience may be upgraded to a mage, putting him one step closer to becoming the even more powerful archmage. This upgrade requires the unit be at least 3rd level. Mages have access to stronger spells that Adepts. More importantly, they lock their natural affinity for at least once dominion of magic. This allows even more powerful versions of the spells in those spheres and causes the unit's combat strength to scale upwards with increading supplies of that type of mana.

A player may have only 7 Archmages at once. A Mage must be at least level 7 before it can be upgraded to an Archmage. Becoming an Archmage is the highest honor most Adepts or Mages could ever imagine. Politically it means being placed over the Mage Guilds of an entire nation. To reach this rank, Archamges must demonstrate the discipline and strength of will to fully master a dominion and cast the strongest spells their affinities allow. This talent also lets Archamges learn to wield weaker versions of every other spell sphere, with enough mana and experience. If an Archmage aspires to gain new affinties, there are 3 possibilities. He can use the Tower of Necromancy to transform himself into a Lich, at level 10 or higher. He can turn to The Ashen Veil, taking on an Unholy Taint and Making a Demonic Pact to share the affinity of a Demon Lord. Lastly, he can use the Tower of Mastery and a lot of experience to let him learn affinity for any sort of mana.

Moroi are men who drink the blood of vampires. This small taste vampiric power gives them enhanced strength and speed, and a feeling of invulnerability beyond that of their still-mortal form. The Calabim often make Moroi out of those they wish to sacrifice in combat. A Moroi who serves particularly well and survives the various suicide missions on which he is sent is occasionally gifted with true vampirism. Moroi can Receive this gift while only at level 3, whereas other must wait until level 7 before earning that honor.

[TAB]"Rifling" is the term describing the practice of putting helical grooves in the barrel of a "long gun" to impart a spin to the projectile. This spin greatly increases the bullet's accuracy at distance. [PARAGRAPH:2]Early long guns, like the Arquebus, were "smoothbores"; these lacked rifling and the bullets were significantly smaller than the barrels of the weapons. When fired, the projectile would bounce against the sides of the weapon's barrel, giving it an uncertain direction upon exiting the barrel. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Khazad began experimenting with muskets using grooved barrels and tighter-fitting projectiles halfway through of the Age of Rebirth, but mass-produced rifled muskets did not appear until the Age of Innovation after the Bannor reclaimed their old capital of Braduk the Burning and built the Foundry of Vengeance to honor Sarabride. The rifled musket was the standard infantry weapon during Matronae purges, while Cavalry officers prided themselves on their rifled pistols.

All of mankind, with the dread exception of the followers of the Undertow, have always strongly resented slavery, on the grounds that no being should be completely subject to another. Oddly enough, this view has never been put forth in regard to Man's fellow animals...-Selena Yera, Elven Mystic

[TAB]Only Agares knows the origin of these stones. They may be a pale reflection of the gems of creation or Agares's failed attempts to make his own. Regardless, they radiate powerful death magic and draw wraiths to them like silent beacons. During the Age of Magic necromancers were said to have turned the stones into powerful weapons for those that wielded them, but only during the Age of Rebirth were they made into weapons that could wield themselves. [PARAGRAPH]The Luchuirp shun demons such as Eidola, yet their Artificers have crafted abominations even more vile. The Enchantments that bring this golem to life also enhance the power of necromancy inherent in the material, creating soulless automata with affinity for Undeath magic. These machines have no wills of their and are not bound by the compact, yet the taint of hell remains within them and lets them summon Imps, Balors, and to channel the power of any Demon Lords with whom their masters have formed Pacts.

Instead of Eidola, the most evil of the Lurchirp command soulless machines whose building materials just happen to come from hell. The Compact did not anticipate Golems with powers like those of true demons, so these abominations are free to enter event Hallowed Ground. Sheut Stone Golems are harder to get than Eidola are though, as they require Sheut Stone mined from Hell terrain as well as a Sculter's Studio.

Frydwell have all the abilities of the Horse Archers that they replace, but no longer functionally identical. These most reclusive of elves now start with [LINK=PROMOTION_FOREST_STEALTH]Forest Stealth[\\LINK] (letting them to hide in [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST]Forests[\\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST_ANCIENT]Ancient Forests[\\LINK], or [LINK=FEATURE_JUNGLE]Jungles[\\LINK]. ) and [LINK=PROMOTION_SUBDUE_ANIMAL]Subdue Animal[\\LINK]. They still require [LINK=BONUS_DEER]Deer[\\LINK] instead of [LINK=BONUS_HORSE]Horses[\\LINK].

Nyxkin get defensive bonuses, have no resource requirement, and can use [LINK=PROMOTION_FOREST_STEALTH]Forest Stealth[\\LINK] to hide in [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST]Forests[\\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST_ANCIENT]Ancient Forests[\\LINK], or [LINK=FEATURE_JUNGLE]Jungles[\\LINK]. They have +1 Poision damage, making them stronger than normal Horse Archers, but do not have the ranged attack ability of the unit they replace.

Also called an Altar Dragon as it prefers sacrifices. They usually have a pool of blood nearby to drink from, and if their servants don't keep it filled they will usually find themselves added to it. Blood Dragons can take human form, and usually prefer to form of a dark nobleman, always with a goblet in hand. The roar of a Blood Dragon vomits up thousands of blood covered, biting, clawing, flying and venomous creatures, a torrent of creatures that are a mix between bats and scorpions. Blood Dragons maintain a collection of perfectly preserved body parts of their victims, skin, faces, organs, all displayed in a place the dragon can admire.

Coral dragons are not a single organism, but a collection of thousands of fist sized insect like creatures called Coralites all working together. They can separate and come back together freely. When they are together they have a breath weapon of white light that resurrects any newly dead (before their soul was collected) that it touches. Even to the point of breathing on a battlefield and raising all the fallen. Coralites occasionally get separated from their colony and have befriended humans as minor pets as they try to work out how to make it back. Coral Dragons collect precious stones, though they will occasionally leave them on the graves of those they respect.

These horned dragons glow with sunlight at all times, though they can control the intensity, from an angelic glow to a blinding golden light. Their breath weapon is a blast of light that burns the corrupt but won't harm the pure. Any ally touched by the light of a Dawn Drake is filled with incredible courage and hope. At dawn each day every Dawn Drake is fully healed from all injuries, mental, physical or magical and is broken free of any constraints that may hold them. They collect anything made of gold.

The largest of the dragons, Elder Dragons tower over castles and most giants. They are typically avoided by other dragons and most lair together in one remote location, the valley of seven pines, where the gods gathered to forge the compact. These dragons met Kylorin when he came to the valley, and allowed him to take the godslayer with him when he left. He occasionally returns and spends years with the Elder Dragons. Although all dragons are immune to mortal magic, Elder Dragons are even immune to the power of the gods (this was given to them as part of the compact, that they might enforce its commands). The roar of an elder dragon fractures creation, permanently leaving fissures of nothingness in the area. Elder Dragons don't collect anything, but they have a fondness for children of all species and are typically kind to them.

Also known as Fang Dragons or Lode Wyrms, these are the only flightless dragons. A Chthonic Dragon can pass through stone and are four times as heavy as it's significant size would indicate. It is quick on land, but when passing through earth it's almost instantaneous. It has no breath weapon, but it's bite easily cuts through stone and metal alike. Flesh and bone are little more than water to them. Chthonic Dragons can control a powerful magnetic field around their body, either attracting, or repulsing metal. Chthonic Dragon teeth, horns and scales are prized by enchanters and crafters. But priests of Kilmorph consider them sacred. Chthonic Dragons collect large gemstones and can be bribed for safe passage with a gem of unusual beauty.
